title: Mock Neck Dress Sewing Pattern – Free PDF
content:
Garment Fitted mock neck midi dress with long sleeves

Level Intermediate

Sizes US 00 – 22 (XXS – 4XL)

Fabric Ponte, double knit, scuba crepe, heavy jersey or firm rib knit

Pieces 6

This free mock neck dress sewing pattern makes a sleek, close-fitting midi dress with a 3 cm stand collar, long fitted sleeves and a straight skirt that falls to mid-calf. It is drafted for stable knits like ponte, has no darts at all, and closes with two invisible zippers, so it looks simple and polished from every side.

→ Jump to the free download

1 cm (3/8″) seam allowance included on all pieces · 2 cm (3/4″) hem on the dress and sleeves · invisible zippers 20 cm (8″) and 30 cm (12″)

Design details of the mock neck dress

The front and the back are each cut in one long piece from the shoulder to the hem, so the shape comes only from the side seams and the centre back seam: there is not a single dart. The mock neck is a real collar stand, interfaced and finished inside with a front and back neck facing, and it opens at the back with one small button above the zipper.

Reading the sketch

On the front, the double curved line at the neck is the collar stand: the inner lines are the inside of the stand seen from the front, with the short vertical lines marking the centre back opening. The long curved lines from the shoulders are the set-in sleeve seams, and the curves at the sides show the shaped side seams, not darts.

On the back, the long line in the middle is the centre back seam. The short cross line below the collar marks the end of the invisible zipper, and the small circle at the top of the stand is the button. There is no slit and no vent in the skirt.

  • Mock neck collar stand, 3 cm (1 1/4″) high, with a one-button back closure
  • Neckline finished inside with a front and back neck facing
  • Long fitted set-in sleeves with a 2 cm (3/4″) hem
  • No darts: the fit comes from the side seams and the centre back seam
  • Centre back seam with a 20 cm (8″) invisible zipper at the neck
  • Invisible 30 cm (12″) zipper in the left side seam
  • Straight midi skirt, about 120 cm (47 1/2″) from the back neck

It is a timeless dress for the office, dinners and cold days, and a good next step if you already sew knit tops: you will learn a collar stand with a facing, two invisible zippers and set-in sleeves in a stable knit.

Sizing guide

Measure your bust around the fullest part and pick the size from the table, then check your waist and hips. This dress is close fitting: between two sizes, choose the larger one. Not sure how to measure? See how to take body measurements and how to choose your sewing pattern size.

US sizes 00 to 22, drafted for a height of 167.75 cm (5 ft 6 in). Letter sizes are a guide only: 00 = XXS · 0–2 = XS · 4–6 = S · 8–10 = M · 12–14 = L · 16 = XL · 18 = 2XL · 20 = 3XL · 22 = 4XL. Always choose by measurements.

Body measurements

Finished dress measurements

The dress has about 3 to 4 cm (1 1/4 to 1 1/2″) of ease at the bust, waist and hips. Lengths are measured at the centre back without seam allowances; the upper arm and sleeve opening are the full width around one sleeve.

Fabric amounts

Estimated with every piece laid out single layer for each size (the front is cut whole), plus about 8 % for shrinkage and straightening. Buy a little more for a one-way print and pre-wash the fabric before cutting.

Common fit adjustments

Length. The skirt ends at mid-calf and is straight, so you can shorten the Front and both Backs by the same amount at the hem for a knee-length dress. Full guide: how to lengthen or shorten a sewing pattern.

Walking room. The skirt is a slim straight column. For a longer stride, leave the lower 25 to 30 cm (10 to 12″) of the centre back seam open as a walking slit and topstitch the seam allowances back.

Materials

  • Main fabric: 1.6 to 2.9 m (1 3/4 to 3 1/4 yd) of a stable knit with 20 to 40 % stretch and good recovery
  • Interfacing: 0.3 m (3/8 yd) of knit (stretch) fusible interfacing for the collar and facings
  • Zippers: one invisible zipper 20 cm (8″) and one invisible zipper 30 cm (12″)
  • Button: one 1 cm (3/8″) button for the collar
  • Tools: ballpoint or stretch needle, invisible zipper foot, twin needle for the hems (optional)
  • Fusible stay tape for the zipper seams (optional), pins or clips, chalk

Pattern pieces

  • 1 Front: cut 1 on a single layer (drawn whole)
  • 2 Back: cut 2
  • 3 Sleeve: cut 2
  • 4 Front Neck Facing: cut 1 + 1 in interfacing
  • 5 Back Neck Facing: cut 2 + 2 in interfacing
  • 6 Back Closure Collar Stand: cut 2 + 2 in interfacing (drawn whole)

Choosing fabric for a mock neck dress

This dress needs a stable knit with 20 to 40 % crosswise stretch and good recovery. Ponte di Roma gives the smooth, matte look of our black version and holds the collar stand upright; double knit and scuba crepe are just as good, and a heavyweight jersey or a firm rib knit make a softer, cosier dress for winter.

A medium-weight woven with 3 to 5 % elastane can work thanks to the two zippers, but the fit will be closer: size up and test the bodice first. More tips in how to choose fabric for sewing patterns and how to sew stretch fabrics.

  2. How to choose your size: which measurement to follow, and what to do between sizes.

Sewing notes

Fit and style

A close fit with 3 to 4 cm of ease and no darts. Baste the side seams and try the dress on before the side zipper if you are between sizes.

Fabric

Stable knits only, or a stretch woven sized up. Use a ballpoint needle and a narrow zigzag or stretch stitch, and do not stretch the seams.

Zippers

Two invisible zippers, at the back neck and in the left side seam. See how to sew a zipper.

Get the pattern

Free PDF pattern, one file per size, US sizes 00 to 22 (XXS to 4XL). Share your make with #sewcraftly!

Download A4
Download US Letter

Print page 1 at 100% and check that the test square measures 10 cm (4 in). New to PDF patterns? Read how to print and assemble a PDF pattern.

Sewing steps

Seam allowance 1 cm (3/8″) unless stated otherwise. Sew right sides together with a narrow zigzag, a stretch stitch or an overlocker, and press every seam before it is crossed by another one.

  1. Prepare. Fuse knit interfacing to the front neck facing, both back neck facings and both collar stand pieces. Staystitch the neckline 8 mm from the edge, and finish the centre back edges and the left side seam edges where the zippers go.
  2. Shoulders. Sew the front to the two backs at the shoulders, finish the seam allowances and press them open.
  3. Collar stand. Sew the two stand pieces right sides together along the upper edge and both short ends, trim, turn and press. Make the buttonhole and sew the button at the marks, then baste the stand to the neckline, matching the centre front, the shoulder seams and the centre back marks.
  4. Back zipper. Insert the 20 cm invisible zipper in the centre back seam from the neck to the ZIP mark, then sew the rest of the centre back seam down to the hem.
  5. Neck facing. Join the front and back neck facings at the shoulders and finish the outer edge. Sew the facing over the collar stand along the neckline, trim, clip and understitch, then turn it inside, turn in the ends at the zipper and slipstitch them to the zipper tape.
  6. Side seams. Sew the right side seam from the underarm to the hem. Sew the left side seam above and below the ZIP marks, leaving about 24 cm open.
  7. Side zipper. Insert the 30 cm invisible zipper in the left side opening, closed at both ends, and stitch the tape ends to the seam allowances.
  8. Sleeves. Easestitch the sleeve caps, sew the underarm seams and hem the sleeves 2 cm (3/4″). Set each sleeve into its armhole, matching the notches and the top notch to the shoulder seam.
  9. Hem. Try the dress on, finish the lower edge, turn up 2 cm (3/4″) and stitch with a twin needle or a narrow zigzag. Give the dress a final press with a pressing cloth on the collar.

Tips and common mistakes

A collar that flops. Interface both stand pieces with knit interfacing and trim the seam allowances inside the stand, so it stays upright without feeling stiff.

Wavy zipper seams. Knits stretch while you sew the zippers. Press a strip of fusible stay tape on the seam allowances first and let the machine feed the fabric.

A facing that rolls out. Understitch the facing as far as you can, tack it to the shoulder seams and press the neckline with a pressing cloth.

A tight fit at the hips. Baste the side seams and try the dress on before inserting the side zipper; with only 3 to 4 cm of ease, a fabric with less stretch may need the next size.

How to style a mock neck dress

Office: in black or charcoal ponte with a long wool coat, pointed flats or ankle boots and small earrings.

Evening: with heeled boots, gold jewellery and a slim belt at the waist. For a softer neckline, try our free square neck midi dress sewing pattern.

Weekend: in a rib knit with white sneakers and a denim jacket, or compare it with our free puff sleeve midi dress sewing pattern for a woven option.

Care

Wash at 30 °C on a gentle cycle, inside out, with both zippers closed. Dry flat or on a hanger, never in the tumble dryer, and press on low heat with a pressing cloth over the collar.

Questions

Is seam allowance included?

Yes: 1 cm (3/8″) on every seam, and a 2 cm (3/4″) hem on the dress and on both sleeves.

Which paper sizes are included?

The free download has A4 and US Letter files, one file per size, so you only print the size you need.

Which size should I choose?

Choose by your bust measurement in the size chart, then check your waist and hips. The dress is close fitting, with about 3 to 4 cm (1 1/4 to 1 1/2″) of ease. Between two sizes, take the larger one.

Can I sew it in a woven fabric?

It is drafted for stable knits such as ponte. A woven with 3 to 5 % elastane also works thanks to the two invisible zippers, but the fit will be closer: choose one size up and make a test bodice first.

Why are there two zippers?

A short 20 cm (8″) invisible zipper at the centre back lets the collar open over your head, and a 30 cm (12″) invisible zipper in the left side seam lets the fitted waist pass over the bust and hips. Both disappear in the seams.

Is this mock neck dress hard to sew?

It is an intermediate project. There are only six pieces and no darts, but you will sew a collar stand with a neck facing, two invisible zippers and set-in sleeves in a knit.

Can I make it shorter?

Yes. The pattern is drafted for a height of 167.75 cm (5 ft 6 in) and ends at mid-calf. The skirt is straight, so you can shorten it at the hem for a knee-length dress without changing anything else.
